newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ramos condemns killing of Filipino journalist.
newsitem.headline: Ramos condemns killing of Filipino journalist.

text.p: President Fidel Ramos on Tuesday condemned the murder of a Filipino journalist as "a dastardly crime against the nation" and vowed to bring the killers to justice.

Police said they had made no arrests and had not established the motive behind the killing of veteran broadcast editor Alberto Berbon, who was shot dead by two assassins on Sunday outside his house in Cavite province just south of Manila.

More than 50 members of media have been killed in the Philippines in the past 20 years, most of them during the martial law regime of late president Ferdinand Marcos. Berbon was the second to die by an assassin's hand this year.

"We raise our voices in condemning this outrage and dastardly crime against him, his family and the nation," Ramos said in the text of his letter of condolence to the Berbon family. "Rest assured that the government will do everything it can to bring to the bar of justice those responsible for his death."
Incidents such as Berbon's murder should "strengthen our resolve to fight together against criminality and violence," he added.
Ramos has created a special team composed of various police agencies to solve the crime, the presidential palace said.
Berbon was senior editor at DZMM radio station, a part of ABS-CBN Broadcasting Corp, which owns the country's biggest television station.
He was also a member of the Crusade Against Violence, a crime monitoring group formed by families of people who have died violently.
